Shader Lab

The Reef's all-in-one ReefLit shader. Change how it switches its 10 features on, and watch two prices at once: cycles per pixel (GPU time) and variants built (build time and size).

Coral Garden, mid-range phone. Goal: GPU ≤ 28 ms, at most 100 shader variants in the build, and the coral glows at night.

Lesson 026: shader cost and variant explosion

    
    
  
    

  
    
    
    What this shows
    
    
    
      
    × 0 is not free
    A feature switched off with a slider still runs on every pixel. In v1 every look pays 35 cycles; each cycle on every ReefLit pixel is 0.6 ms.
    
      
    Keywords double
    Every on/off keyword doubles the variants that multi_compile builds: 12 keywords, 4,096 copies, 41 minutes. The game uses 24.
    
      
    Pick the price per feature
    Set once on a material: shader_feature. Changed by a script and cheap: a uniform branch. Changed by a script and expensive: multi_compile.
    
    
    
    
    This lab is a simulation, not a measurement. It uses the lesson's numbers: ReefLit covers 1,440,000 fragments, so 1 cycle = 0.6 ms; the other stations are vertex 15, raster 5.3, memory 23 ms, plus 12 ms of other pixel work and 3 ms fixed. Each variant takes 0.6 s and 30 KB, for one pass on one platform. Real compilers report cycles per unit (arithmetic, texture, load/store), real engines multiply variants by passes and graphics APIs, and a uniform branch's cost varies by GPU.
